To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

chordomas are positive for the majority of the active proteins in the PI3k/AKT/TSC2/m-TOR pathway, and that the majority of chordomas are positive by immunohistochemical staining for m-TOR and/or p70 S6K.

(1) 65% of chordomas are potentially amenable to treatment with mTOR inhibitors, (2) the PI3K-AKT-mTOR signalling pathway is active in chordoma and (3) combined therapy with drugs that inhibit AKt may be beneficial in chordoma patients.

Chordoma, a rare, radio- and chemotherapy-resistant tumour of bone, is associated with activation of the PI3K-AKT-TSC1/TSC1-mTOR-p70S6-K pathway and loss of PTEN, which is associated with activation and overexpression of p-AKT, p-TSC2, p-p70S-6K, p-RPS6, p-4E- BP1, eIF4-E, and mTOR.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the PI3K/PTEN/AKT/TSC/mTOR signalling pathway and the potential therapeutic targets that may be used in chordoma treatment.
the identification of potential targets for the treatment and/or prevention of the development of chordoma.
the identification of molecular targets for chordoma therapy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
chordoma is characterised by a high frequency of activation of the PI3K pathway, and that the most promising therapeutic targets would be mTOR and AKT inhibitors, alone or in combination.
92% of the chordoma cases analysed may respond to inhibitors of PI3K/Akt/TSC1/TSc2/mTOR signalling, including inhibitors of the mTOR complex 2.
the PI3KCA/AKT/TSC2/mTor/p70S6K signalling pathway is active in chordoma and that it may represent a target for therapy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
chordoma cells harbour constitutive activation of the PI3K-AKT-TSC1/TSC-mTOR pathway and that this may be a potential therapeutic target.

the PI3KCA/RHEB1/mTOR pathway is activated in chordomas and that the mTOR inhibitors, which are already available in clinical practice, may be useful as therapeutic agents in the treatment of chordomas, especially in combination with AKT inhibitors, which are currently being developed.
the PI3KCA/AKT/TSC2/RPS6/mTOR pathway is activated in chordomas.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the PI3K pathway may be a promising molecular target for the development of novel therapies for chordoma.
the PI3K-AKT-TSC1-TSC2-mTOR signalling pathway is activated in chordomas and that this activation is a potential target for therapeutic intervention.
chordomas have an active PI3K/Akt/TSC1/TSc2/mTOR pathway with a significant percentage of cases having loss of PTEN and mTOR.
